rationale: The agent correctly authenticated the user via full name and zip, identified the correct DC-shipping order, and successfully modified the backpack and desk lamp variants. However, it made several policy violations and did not fully complete the user’s request: (1) It performed order-changing writes (item modifications) without first stating the exact changes and obtaining explicit user confirmation. (2) It unilaterally chose a payment method (the user’s gift card) in the modification call without confirming the payment method. (3) It failed to complete the requested address change; moreover, the agent’s sequence (modifying items first) appears to have advanced the order from pending to non-pending, blocking the address update that was part of the original request. (4) The explanation that “after an item modification no further changes are allowed” was misleading; the tool error indicated the order was non-pending, not a blanket policy about post-modification restrictions. (5) The agent did not offer appropriate alternatives (e.g., cancellation/reorder or escalation) once the address change was blocked. These issues violate the requirement to confirm before writes, avoid unsupported statements, and complete the user’s requested changes when permitted.
